name: Whisperer
subtitle: Plan-derived MCM dining table
description: A parametric 1:10 solid-oak model of the 72 × 40 inch mid-century dining table: a deeply beveled 1 3/4 inch top, four 15-degree splayed and tapered legs, a recessed four-apron frame, and four independent leveling feet.

dimensionTargets: The tabletop is 72 in long by 40 in wide by 1 3/4 in thick, with a 5 in underside bevel that leaves a 1/2 in perimeter edge.

Four 1 3/4 in thick legs splay at 15 degrees and taper from 4 in at the top to 2 3/8 in at the foot; direct-contact legs use 29 1/4 in blanks and enabled feet shorten the wood while preserving overall height.
The leg-foot corner chamfers are 1/2 in at the floor and taper to zero toward the top.
Four independently adjustable 1 1/2 in pads use 3/8 in threaded rods and a default 3/4 in installed extension while preserving the 30 in overall height.
Two 52 1/4 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2 in long aprons use 18-degree end details and a 45-degree bottom chamfer.
Two 25 1/2 × 4 × 1 1/2 in side aprons follow the 15-degree leg assembly and use a 30-degree bottom-edge chamfer.
All four aprons are recessed 1/4 in from the leg faces.
invariants: Keep the full-size furniture dimensions independent from the mock scale denominator.
Keep the tabletop, each leg, and every apron as a closed printable solid.
Keep the four legs mirrored in pairs and preserve the 15-degree longitudinal splay; shorten the wood below the apron when leveling feet are enabled so the tabletop height does not change.
Keep each foot inside the 72 × 40 in tabletop plan envelope at the default dimensions.
Keep the apron tops registered to the tabletop underside and the apron faces recessed from the leg faces.
Keep the top underside bevel centered and leave a positive flat center field.
Treat the PDF as the dimensional source while leaving joinery that is not dimensioned in the plan out of the visual model.

Keep structural scores tied to the Whisperer's four-apron frame, splayed contact footprint, beveled top, and selected floor-contact system; do not reuse the Plate Table's apronless steel-plate assumptions.
With leveling feet enabled, keep four separate pads on Z = 0, keep every rod centered under its leg, retain positive rod embedment, and export the registered hardware separately from the wood.
Treat the structural panel as a geometry-only comparison and require full-size joint, rocking, lateral-push, deflection, and repeated-load tests before build approval.
Export registered support-free wood and hardware STLs while leveling feet are enabled; disabling them restores the original one-piece wood export and direct wood floor contact.
